name: Hello
author: brodgar
description: Example addon + standing regression harness — runs in the Lua sandbox (self-checks it at OnLoad; READ-ONLY (declares no permissions), so it is default-enabled and needs no consent — the gated hafen.act write tier now lives in the separate, opt-in 'walker' addon, which declares 'permissions': ['actions'] and is therefore disabled by default, its enabling gated by a per-addon consent dialog with no global switch — D-027/D-028) over the event bus, timers, saved variables (hafen.store), custom UI (hafen.ui — a draggable window, a HUD overlay, and world-space gob overlays, all drawn via the GOut wrapper), client-only world ghosts (hafen.ghost — V1: new{res,x,y[,a]} places a virtual prop (a Gob with no server id) in the 3D world and returns a handle with :move/:pos/:res/:clickable/:destroy, list([filter]) lists this addon's live ghosts; SAFE-tier and NOT gated (D-029) since nothing reaches the server; V2 adds opt-in clickability — clickable=true (or :clickable(bool)) gives a ghost a pick surface and a click on it is detected client-side and CONSUMED before any server click (so you never walk/interact — still SAFE-tier, D-032), firing the per-ghost onClick and the owner-scoped GhostClicked{ghost,button,x,y} event; a non-clickable ghost is click-through; V3 adds look & orientation — new{...a=,alpha=,tint=,sdt=} plus the handle verbs :rotate(a)/:setRes(res[,sdt])/:alpha(0..1)/:tint{r,g,b[,a]}/:show()/:hide() (alpha<1 is the translucent 'ghost' look, tint is a colour overlay); at OnEnterWorld the harness spawns a non-clickable log cabin a few tiles away ROTATED and TRANSLUCENT (click-through), reads list()/pos(), moves it, then live-swaps its resource + rotates it, hides & re-shows it, and auto-destroys it after 8s, and ':hello ghost' toggles a CLICKABLE translucent cabin at your position — click it: it logs onClick + GhostClicked, live-rotates + re-fades itself (V3), and you do not move), custom images (hafen.render -- R1: hafen.render.image(path) loads a PNG from THIS addon's own folder into a client-only, bridge-owned TexI handle (paths are addon-relative and sandboxed: absolute / '..' are rejected, D-017) with :size() -> {w,h} and :dispose(); draw it inside any draw callback via the g wrapper: g:image(img,x,y[,w,h]) (native or scaled) and g:aimage(img,x,y,ax,ay) (anchored); SAFE-tier and NOT gated (D-034) since it never reaches the server, and it is disposed AUTOMATICALLY on reload/disable so there is no GL leak; hello loads icon.png at OnLoad and draws it in the 2a window (native 32x32 + scaled 16x16) and the 2b HUD overlay (anchored beside the readout)), custom world sprites (hafen.render -- R2a: hafen.render.sprite{image,x,y[,a,scale,alpha,tint]} stands a custom PNG UPRIGHT in the 3D world as a fixed textured quad -- the non-.res sibling of a ghost, on the SAME client-only virtual-entity core (a Gob with no server id, SAFE-tier and NOT gated, D-034), so it is a transform handle like a ghost: :move/:rotate/:scale/:alpha/:tint/:clickable/:show/:hide/:pos/:image/:destroy, gizmo-compatible, torn down automatically on reload/disable; ':hello sprite' stands the icon.png at your feet (~3 tiles tall) then, 2s later, moves + rotates + scales it to show the live transform, and ':hello sprite' again removes it; R2b adds the CAMERA-FACING BILLBOARD form -- hafen.render.sprite{...,billboard=true} draws the PNG as a screen-space blit at the projected world point so it always faces the camera and stays a constant screen size (position + gizmo-move apply, world-rotate/scale do not), and ':hello billboard' stands one facing you; a FIXED sprite can also be made clickable=true (a billboard has no world mesh, so it is never picked), firing the per-sprite onClick and the owner-scoped SpriteClicked{sprite,button,x,y} event just like a ghost; it can also be ANCHORED to a gob and FOLLOW it every frame -- hafen.render.sprite{follow=<Gob object>, offset={x=,y=,z=}} (z=up) plus the handle verbs :follow(gob[,{x=,y=,z=}])/:offset{x=,y=,z=} (a plain :move detaches), the world-space analog of a gob overlay: ':hello follow' floats icon.png above your head and it follows you as you walk), custom 3D models (hafen.render -- R3a/R3b: hafen.render.model(path) loads a glTF 2.0 STATIC model (.glb preferred, or .gltf + buffers) from THIS addon's folder into a cached, bridge-owned mesh handle (:bounds()->{min,max,size} world units, :info()->{prims,textured,lit,textures,verts,tris}, :dispose()); the pure-Java parser bakes the glTF (+Y up) into H&H model space (Z up; 1 metre = 1 tile) as POSITION + indices with multiple primitives/materials, and R3b decodes TEXCOORD_0 + the baseColorTexture (embedded/data-URI/external PNG-JPG -> shared TexIs owned by the mesh) x baseColorFactor with alpha modes OPAQUE/MASK/BLEND + doubleSided cull, and R3c adds LIGHTING (baked per-vertex normals + a Phong material state, so the model shades with the world lights instead of drawing fullbright; :info().lit counts the lit primitives). hafen.render.object{model,x,y[,a,scale,alpha,tint,clickable,onClick,follow]} then stands the model in the 3D world -- the mesh sibling of a sprite/ghost, on the SAME client-only virtual-entity core (a Gob with no server id, SAFE-tier and NOT gated, D-034), so it is a transform handle like a sprite: :move/:rotate/:scale/:alpha/:tint/:clickable/:show/:hide/:pos/:mesh/:destroy, gizmo-compatible, torn down automatically on reload/disable; hello loads tank.glb (a real textured, multi-material model) at OnLoad (logging its prim/texture counts) and ':hello object' stands it TEXTURED at your feet -- scaled from :bounds() to ~2 tiles tall -- then, 2s later, moves + rotates + grows it to show the live transform on a mesh, and ':hello object' again removes it), widget-creation interception (hafen.ui.onWidgetCreate — observes every server window the client builds and logs its {id,type,place,caption,parentType} descriptor), widget models (hafen.ui.adopt — adopts the main inventory as a hidden model: the 'bags' hotkey hides/shows its grid while it stays live, with items() reads and onItemAdded/onItemRemoved/onDestroy events; un-hides on reload/disable), map markers (hafen.markers — reads the on-disk map DB with list/nearest, and the 'marker' hotkey drops/removes a persistent 'Hello marker' at your position; MarkersChanged fires on changes), radar/minimap icons (hafen.radar — reads the gob-icon categories with categories() -> {name,res,show,notify}, and can setVisible/setNotify per filter; read-only in this addon since the setters persist to your real icon settings), kin/buddy roster (hafen.kin -- CALLABLE-ONLY and OOP since 020-kin-oop: hafen.kin() is the ROSTER (an array of interned Kin objects in Kin-window sort order, plus :find(nameOrId), :list([filter]) whose function filter receives a Kin, and the gated :add(secret)) and hafen.kin(idOrName) is ONE Kin object -- :id/:name/:group/:color (nil above the client's 8-colour palette)/:online/:exists/:info (the flat snapshot escape hatch) -- with the gated verbs :rename/:setGroup(0..254)/:endkin/:forget each returning self so they chain; the old FLAT table (list/find/add/remove/forget/rename/setGroup as fields on the namespace) is GONE (hard cut, D-013). KinChanged fires when a kin is added/removed or flips online/offline, and hello names who just came online; hello is read-only here since the write verbs are the gated action tier), movement speed (hafen.speed — reads the crawl/walk/run/sprint selector with get() -> current 0..3, max() -> highest selectable, name([n]) -> display name; read-only since changing speed is the gated Phase-4 tier), crafting (hafen.craft — reads the open recipe/craft window with current() -> {recipe, inputs, outputs, qmod, tools} (inputs/outputs are {res,name,num,opt} specs; qmod/tools are {res,name} arrays), or nil when none is open; read at login (usually 'none') and via ':hello craft' which dumps the recipe you currently have open; read-only since craft.make is the gated Phase-4 tier, and there is no CraftChanged event — read on demand), quest log (hafen.quests — reads the character sheet's Quest Log with list([filter]) -> {id,name,res,status,mtime} for both the Current and Completed tabs, and selected() -> the open quest plus its conds={{desc,status,text}} objectives; QuestAdded fires when a new active quest appears and QuestDone when one is completed/failed, and ':hello quest' dumps the selected quest's objectives; read-only since there is no quest action tier), wounds (hafen.wounds — reads the character sheet's Health & Wounds tab with list([filter]) -> {id,name,res,severity,parentid,level} (wounds form a tree via parentid; severity is the magnitude the client shows beside a wound) and has(needle); WoundChanged fires when a wound is added/healed or its severity changes, and ':hello wound' dumps the full wound tree; read-only since wounds heal by playing/tending), combat schools (hafen.fight — reads the character sheet's Martial Arts & Combat Schools tab, the OUT-OF-COMBAT maneuver-deck builder: maneuvers([filter]) -> {res,name,avail,used} for every known maneuver/attack, deck() -> the current school's configured card layout {slot,key,res,name,used} for the filled hotkey slots, and summary() -> {maxact,used,nact,nsave,usesave} (the action-point budget + active saved-school slot); read at login and via ':hello fight' which dumps the deck by hotkey plus your known maneuvers; read-only since editing/switching schools is the gated Phase-4 tier, and there is no FightChanged event — read on demand), global hotkeys (hafen.client:options():keybindings():register — 'toggle' shows/hides the window, plus 'ping', 'bags' and 'marker'; all start UNBOUND under a 'Hello' section in Options > Keybindings, where you assign the keys), slash commands (hafen.slash.register — a WoW-style ':hello' console command with sub-commands 'toggle'/'ping'/'echo'; args come in as a 1-based table; reload-safe via a single engine-lifetime dispatcher, so :reload swaps the handler with no duplicate/leaked command — coverage-gaps C1), JSON (hafen.json — self-checks encode/parse at OnLoad: hafen.json.encode(value) -> compact JSON (strict — a function/userdata/cycle/non-finite number is a pcall-able error, so output is always valid JSON) and hafen.json.parse(str) -> Lua value (objects -> string-keyed tables, arrays -> 1-based; JSON null -> nil = an ABSENT key / array hole; integral numbers -> Lua ints; malformed input or over the size/depth caps -> a pcall-able error), the harness round-trips a mixed table and verifies the null->nil caveat + integer cleanliness; ungated pure CPU, D-036), input hooks (hafen.hook.input — a MapView mousedown pre-hook that cancels map clicks while 'map-lock' is on), action hooks (hafen.hook.action — a MapView 'click' pre-hook that intercepts a move and re-sends it while 'move-intercept' is on), message hooks (hafen.hook.message — an IMeter 'set' pre-hook that swallows meter updates so the HUD meter bars freeze while 'meter-freeze' is on), and the read API (hafen.gob(id) -- the Gob CLASS: hafen.gob(id) mints an interned Gob OBJECT and gob:pos()/:name()/:health()/:distance()/:info()/... read it live (the flat hafen.gob.*(ref) accessor and the "player"/"me"/"partyN" GobRef tokens are GONE -- hard cut, D-044; the player's gob is hafen.player():gob()), hafen.world.* (gobs/nearest/within hand out Gob objects), hafen.map.*, hafen.player() -- the Player object (:gob()/:name()/:worldToScreen(), D-046; :vitals() is GONE, the HUD bars are hafen.meter now), hafen.time.*, hafen.sound() -- CALLABLE-ONLY and OOP since 024-audio-oop: hafen.sound(name) is one interned Sound (:res/:play([volume])/:stop/:playing/:info, volume being the FIRST argument of the play call and never entity state, D-059) and hafen.sound() with no argument is the array of the Sounds THIS addon still has in the air (auto-silenced on disable/:reload); the flat hafen.sound.play is GONE (hard cut, D-013) and there is NO hafen.music at all (D-058 -- haven.Music is MIDI and this server sends none; what you hear as music is ambient audio, i.e. Options > Audio > 'Ambient volume'), hafen.items.*, hafen.char.* incl. food/skills/credos/experiences, hafen.party.*, hafen.buff() -- CALLABLE-ONLY and OOP since 025-buffs-oop: hafen.buff() is the 1-based array of Buff objects on the buff bar (in bar order; a buff the server has just removed is already out, even while it fades on screen) and hafen.buff(needle) is the FIRST whose res or name contains it (the old buffs.has() predicate, now handing back the object; a miss is plain nil, a NUMBER key errors), each object reading live per call (:res/:name/:amount/:duration/:number/:exists/:info, with amount/duration 0..1 fractions and NOT seconds (:duration() is the radial meter -- the share of the buff's run still left)) and interned per addon, so a REMOVED buff still answers its reads with :exists() false -- which is what makes the BuffAdded/BuffRemoved/BuffChanged payload, now the Buff OBJECT itself, worth stashing; the flat hafen.buffs (list/has) is GONE (hard cut, D-013) --, hafen.meter() -- CALLABLE-ONLY and OOP since 027-meters-oop: hafen.meter() is the 1-based array of every bar in the HUD's meter slot (in HUD order -- NOT a hard-coded hp/stamina/energy triple read by tree position, which is what the old flat hafen.player():vitals() was, and which silently dropped the two extra bars a mount adds) and hafen.meter(needle) is the FIRST whose bg RESOURCE name contains that substring -- the names are SERVER-published (observed here: gfx/hud/meter/{hp,stam,nrj,haest,mount}), so the API searches them and :res() is how you read the real ones off a live client, never a client-side alias dictionary (D-063); each object reads live per call (:res/:index/:value/:color/:segments/:exists/:info, colour and multi-segment bars reaching Lua for the first time) and is interned per addon on the WIDGET identity, so a REMOVED meter still answers with :exists() false -- which is what makes the MeterAdded/MeterRemoved/MeterChanged payload, the Meter OBJECT itself, worth stashing (NB a MeterAdded payload can be younger than its resource: :res() is nil AT FIRE TIME, so name-match on a later tick); hafen.player():vitals(), the Vitals type and VitalsChanged are GONE (hard cut, D-013) --, hafen.study.*, hafen.actionbar() -- CALLABLE-ONLY and OOP since 021-actionbar-oop: hafen.actionbar() is the 1-based array of all 144 Slot objects and hafen.actionbar(n) is ONE Slot at the raw 0-based game index (0..143, out of range throws), reading live per call (:index/:empty/:res/:name/:cooldown/:info) with the gated :use([mods]) returning self; the flat .slot/.use fields are GONE (hard cut, D-013) and ActionbarChanged now carries the changed Slot itself; 022 adds the second gated write slot:set(resourceName), which ASSIGNS an action to a slot by resource name (the wdgmsg a drag from the menu grid sends) and which hello, being read-only, only checks REFUSES -- the working demo is ':walker setbar <n> <res>' --, hafen.radar.*, hafen.kin(), hafen.speed.*, hafen.craft.*, hafen.quests.*, hafen.wounds.*, hafen.fight.*) plus the widget-tree events (MeterAdded/Removed/Changed, BuffAdded/Removed/Changed, FepChanged, StudyChanged, ActionbarChanged, EquipChanged), the map event MarkersChanged, the kin event KinChanged, the quest events QuestAdded/QuestDone, the wound event WoundChanged, and the world-entity click events GhostClicked (ghosts) and SpriteClicked (fixed sprites). U1 adds three additive UI primitives exercised by a borderless drop-target widget below the 2a window: onDrop (D-038 -- the widget implements DropTarget, so dragging a menu-grid action onto it fires onDrop(x,y,{kind='pagina',res='<name>'}), a neutral ungated descriptor; a truthy return consumes the drop), g:resource(name,x,y[,w,h]) (D-039 -- draws an ENGINE .res image by name, the sibling of g:image for the addon's own PNGs; async + cached + Loading-guarded, used to render the dropped action's real icon), and the trailing mods={shift,ctrl,alt} table now carried by onClick/onMouseUp/onMouseMove/onWheel (D-040 -- Shift+click the box and the log shows shift=true). ':hello prof' exercises 019.4: it runs a gob scan through p:measure('scan-gobs', fn) and a loop inside an explicit p:scope('spin'):begin()/:finish() pair -- both no-ops with the profiling checkbox off -- then dumps p:addons() (per-addon ms/avg/peak/share, the call breakdown by category, and this addon's named scopes) plus the total row, which is the same number p:frame().addons reports. ':hello widgets' exercises 019.5: p:widgets() breaks the UI half of the frame down per widget TYPE and per individual widget -- tickMs/drawMs are inclusive of children and selfMs is that minus them (a widget is timed by its parent, around the call that ticks/draws its whole subtree), the total row is the root widget inclusive tick+draw so every rows self time sums to it, and an addon-owned widget (hello own panel is a LuaWidget) carries an owner id so the same cost shows up itemised here and rolled up in that addon p:addons() row. ':hello passes' exercises 019.6: p:passes() reports a fixed, curated list of named render passes -- shadow (the whole shadow-map render), scene (the 3D draw list) and ui2d (the widget tree) -- with CPU and GPU time SIDE BY SIDE, so 'what do shadows cost me' is a number: turn Video > Shadows off and the shadow row falls to zero while the GPU frame time drops by about what it had been reporting. The rows are DISJOINT (shadow and scene run inside the widget draw, since the MapView is a widget, so each row is self time -- its span minus the passes nested in it, exactly like p:widgets()), which is why the three sum to less than the GPU frame instead of double-counting the scene, and why ui2d means the 2D UI. Every pass boundary is a real GL timestamp query, so the list is short and curated forever -- per-draw-call GPU attribution is RenderDoc territory and out of scope. The same command dumps p:gl(), the ARMED-ONLY submission counters (drawCalls / programBinds / vertices / triangles): unlike p:render(), which merely exposes numbers the client already keeps and therefore answers with profiling off, nothing counts these, so they are new counting behind the master switch. ':hello textcache' exercises 026.2: p:textcache() reports the rendered-text cache g:text/g:atext draw through -- entries, GL texture bytes held, hits, misses, evictions and the hit rate for THIS addon, plus the two caps it is bounded by and a 'total' row summing every Lua owner (which is the leak check: disable every addon and total.bytes goes to ~0, because teardown disposes each cache). It is PULL-ONLY like p:memory()/p:net()/p:loader()/p:render(), i.e. it answers with the profiling checkbox OFF, since every number in it is one the cache keeps anyway in order to bound itself. The HUD overlay draws one STATIC line (rasterised once, a cache hit every frame thereafter) beside one VOLATILE line (its text carries the frame number, so it misses every frame by construction) so both rates are always real, and ':hello textcache stress' toggles the BOUND check: a pool of 2000 distinct strings fed 32 a frame at alpha 0 -- invisible, but rasterised and cached for real -- so entries climb to the cap and STOP, bytes stop with them and evictions start counting.
